numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Integrating a piecewise constant function in nested integrals returns nan for the third nested integral (integrate(f1 * integrate(f2 * integrate(f3, (t3,0,t2)), (t2,0,t1)), (t1,0,3))); a single NaN from one interval evaluation is summed into the whole result and corrupts it even though earlier partial sums were correct. The first two integrals print a1 + a2 + a3 and a1**2/2 + a1*a2 + a1*a3 + a2**2/2 + a2*a3 + a3**2/2 respectively.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The third nested integral should not be nan, since the functions are only evaluated on the interval (0,3) where everything is well-defined; the integral should evaluate to a finite symbolic expression instead of nan.
trigger_conditions: Piecewise function with symbolic integration boundaries, e.g. Piecewise((a1, t<1), (a2, t<2), (a3, t<3)) integrated over intervals split at symbolic limits
Three nested integrals of piecewise constant functions with bounds depending on outer integration variables (t3 from 0 to t2, t2 from 0 to t1, t1 from 0 to 3)
An interval evaluation returns NaN for one of the split sub-intervals and is added into the running sum

input_output_examples.input: from sympy import *; a1, a2, a3 = symbols('a1 a2 a3'); t, t1, t2, t3 = symbols('t t1 t2 t3'); p = [(a1, t<1), (a2, t<2), (a3, t<3)]; f1 = Piecewise(*p).subs({t:t1}); f2 = Piecewise(*p).subs({t:t2}); f3 = Piecewise(*p).subs({t:t3}); integrate(f1 * integrate(f2 * integrate(f3, (t3,0,t2)), (t2,0,t1)), (t1,0,3))
input_output_examples.expected_output: a finite symbolic expression (not nan); the issue gives no exact expected form

input_output_examples.input: integrate(f1, (t1,0,3)) with f1 = Piecewise((a1, t1<1), (a2, t1<2), (a3, t1<3))

oracle_clues: The issue states the first two integrals are correct and only the third should not be nan
The proposed fix checks whether the interval evaluation result is Undefined and, if so, returns Piecewise((sum, hi <= upto), (Undefined, True)) instead of adding it to the sum
Reproducer from issue#28469 is kept whole in the PR discussion; no numeric tolerance is stated

category_specific_evidence: Special value involved is a symbolic NaN (printed as nan) returned when _eval_interval evaluates the antiderivative on a split sub-interval of Piecewise integration; it enters the running sum and corrupts the total.

Issue #28469 reproducer: the third nested integral integrate(f1*integrate(f2*integrate(f3,(t3,0,t2)),(t2,0,t1)),(t1,0,3)) returns nan, while the first two nestings print a1 + a2 + a3 and a1**2/2 + a1*a2 + a1*a3 + a2**2/2 + a2*a3 + a3**2/2 correctly.
The issue states the functions are only evaluated on (0,3) where everything is well-defined, so the NaN is spurious propagation rather than a true singularity.

Correct handling per the diff: when abei[i][-2]._eval_interval(x, a, b) returns Undefined, return Piecewise((sum, hi <= upto), (Undefined, True)) instead of adding it to sum; otherwise add it and set upto = b.
PR description: if a NaN appears, the value integrated up to that point is returned and the result is left undefined after that point.

Regression test test_integration_of_piecewise_with_simbolic_boundaries expects I2 to be a Piecewise with branches for t1 < 0, t1 <= Min(3, t1), and a final (nan, True) branch, and expects integrate(f1*I2,(t1,0,3)) to be a polynomial in a1, a2, a3 with no nan.
No signed zero, subnormal, or +/-inf handling is discussed; the special value concerns only symbolic NaN/Undefined from Piecewise.
reproduction_risks: The passages do not state a numeric dtype or precision; the bug is in SymPy symbolic integration, so IEEE special-value semantics (signed zero, subnormals, +/-inf) are not covered.
The NaN is a SymPy symbolic nan/Undefined, so a reproduction must check the symbolic result (e.g. with .has(nan) or equality to Undefined) rather than a float comparison.
The diff tests for Undefined while the PR text speaks of NaN; the test expects a (nan, True) branch, so these may differ and should be checked against the code.
The regression test expected value is truncated in the passages, so the full expected polynomial should not be assumed.
No numeric tolerance is stated; comparisons are exact symbolic equality in the test.
